definitions.name: g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}
definitions.construction: For \(x\in\mathcal{B}_P\), define the canonical exact-distance regression on \([0,\infty)\) by \[g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)=\begin{cases}N_{t,P,x}(s)/Q_{t,P,x}(s),&s>0\text{ and }Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0,\\ \mu_{t,P}(x),&s=0,\\ \mu_{t,P}(x),&s>0\text{ and }Q_{t,P,x}(s)=0.\end{cases}\]

definitions.name: \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}}
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}}(q,L,c_{-},r_0)=\left\{P:\text{for every }n\in\mathbb{N},\text{ all member properties enumerated below hold}\right\}.\]

definitions.name: \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}}
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}}(q,\iota,L,c_{-},r_0,\rho_0)=\left\{P:\text{for every }n\in\mathbb{N},\text{ all member properties enumerated below hold}\right\}.\]

definitions.name: K_\triangle
definitions.construction: \[K_\triangle(u)=\max\{1-|u|,0\}.\] This fixed kernel is nonnegative, symmetric, Lipschitz, supported on \([-1,1]\), and positive on \((-1,1)\).

definitions.name: \widehat{\tau}^{\mathrm{LC}}_{n,h}
definitions.construction: Define \(\widehat{\mu}_{t,h}(x)=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf{1}\{T_i=t\}K_\triangle(D_{P,x,i}/h)Y_i}{\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf{1}\{T_i=t\}K_\triangle(D_{P,x,i}/h)}\) whenever the denominator is positive, use zero otherwise, and set \(\widehat{\tau}^{\mathrm{LC}}_{n,h}(x)=\widehat{\mu}_{1,h}(x)-\widehat{\mu}_{0,h}(x)\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak{H}_{\mathrm{ang}}
definitions.construction: Coarea angular-density confounding handle: expand each arm-specific radial conditional mean as a ratio of circle-level angular integrals; vary bounded continuous score densities through shrinking-scale angular imbalances while preserving the fixed radial mass envelope; pair those imbalances with disjoint \(q\)-H\"older bump perturbations of affine baselines and bounded or Bernoulli outcomes; and use the induced compressed likelihoods to determine both a separated-center packing and the primitive regularity that prevents such confounding.

statements.justification: The bounded density supplies the upper half of local mass control, so the class needs only the primitive lower-thickness condition.
statements.gap: This is a supporting consequence of the density envelope rather than an additional Ahlfors-type premise.
statements.consumer: The local-constant stochastic bound and its population denominator use this estimate uniformly over boundary points.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}}\), injectivity and \(C^1\) regularity give \[\mathcal{H}^1(\mathcal{B}_P)=\int_0^1\lVert\gamma_P'(u)\rVert_2\,du,\qquad L^{-1}\leq\mathcal{H}^1(\mathcal{B}_P)\leq L.\]
statements.justification: The smooth class obtains its curve-length control from primitive chart conditions rather than a redundant membership assumption.
statements.gap: This standard geometric identity is supporting infrastructure, not a separate statistical contribution.
statements.consumer: The uniform stochastic bound covers the trimmed curve by a number of balls controlled by the derived length envelope.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}\).  The smooth-embedding assumption makes \(\gamma_P\) an injective \(C^1\) map, while the speed assumption gives \(\lVert\gamma_P'(u)\rVert_2>0\) for every \(u\).  Thus the standard change-of-parameter formula for the length of a regular injective curve gives
\[
\mathcal H^1(\mathcal B_P)=\int_0^1\lVert\gamma_P'(u)\rVert_2\,du.
\]
The lower speed bound yields
\[
\mathcal H^1(\mathcal B_P)\geq\int_0^1L^{-1}\,du=L^{-1}.
\]
The chart-derivative envelope includes \(\sup_u\lVert\gamma_P'(u)\rVert_2\leq L\), and hence
\[
\mathcal H^1(\mathcal B_P)
\leq\int_0^1L\,du=L.
\]
All boundary and endpoint conditions are covered by the parameter interval \([0,1]\), so no additional endpoint term occurs.

statements.statement: For the fixed kernel \(K_\triangle\), there is \(\kappa_0=\kappa_0(c_{-},r_0)>0\) such that, for all sufficiently small \(h\), \[\inf_{P\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}}}\inf_{t\in\{0,1\}}\inf_{x\in\mathcal{B}_P}\Psi^{(0)}_{t,P,x}(h)\geq\kappa_0,\qquad \inf_{P\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}}}\inf_{t\in\{0,1\}}\inf_{x\in\mathcal{B}_{P,\delta}}\Psi^{(0)}_{t,P,x}(h)\geq\kappa_0.\]
statements.justification: This theorem-local support verifies denominator stability for the one fixed degree-zero estimator used in both distance upper bounds.
statements.gap: CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance uses a broader high-level Gram condition for local-polynomial upper theory; this lemma derives only the scalar bound needed by the fixed triangular local-constant estimator.
statements.consumer: The rectifiable and smooth distance upper bounds use the same stable estimator without quantifying over kernels or polynomial degrees.
statements.proof_tex:
For \(|u|\leq1/2\), the triangular kernel satisfies \(K_\triangle(u)\geq1/2\).  Let \(0<h\leq2r_0\).  For any law in either displayed class, any permitted boundary point \(x\), and either arm \(t\), deterministic assignment gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Psi^{(0)}_{t,P,x}(h)
&=h^{-2}\mathbb E_P\!\left[K_\triangle(D_{P,x}/h)\mathbf 1\{T=t\}\right]\\
&\geq\frac{1}{2h^2}P\{X\in\mathcal A_{t,P}\cap B_2(x,h/2)\}\\
&\geq\frac{1}{2h^2}c_{-}(h/2)^2
=\frac{c_{-}}8.
\end{aligned}
\]
The last inequality is precisely uniform two-sided thickness, applicable because \(h/2\leq r_0\).  Therefore one may take \(\kappa_0=c_{-}/8\).  The second infimum is over the smaller set \(\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\subseteq\mathcal B_P\), so the same calculation proves it without an endpoint exception.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}}\cup\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}}\), \(x\in\mathcal{B}_P\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), coarea gives, for \(0<r\leq r_0\), \[P\{X\in\mathcal{A}_{t,P}\cap B_2(x,r)\}=\int_0^r Q_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds\geq c_{-}r^2.\] Hence the set \(\{s>0:Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0\}\) accumulates at zero, without requiring positivity at every radius. For Lebesgue-almost every \(s>0\) with \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0\), \(g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)=N_{t,P,x}(s)/Q_{t,P,x}(s)\) is a version of \(\mathbb{E}_P[Y\mid D_{P,x}=(2t-1)s]\). The canonical values on zero-denominator radii satisfy \[|g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)-\mu_{t,P}(x)|\leq Ls,\qquad s\geq0,\] and therefore \[\tau_P(x)=\lim_{s\downarrow0}\bigl(g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{1,P,x}(s)-g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{0,P,x}(s)\bigr).\]
statements.justification: The lemma makes exact-distance conditioning well posed without asserting that every circle has positive arm density and shows that the canonical representative identifies the boundary contrast.
statements.gap: CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance, Theorem 1, supplies the identification background; this supporting lemma makes the coarea version and its behavior on zero-denominator radii explicit for the present primitive classes.
statements.consumer: The two distance-only frontier theorems use this canonical radial regression for their bias calculations and causal interpretation.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\), \(x\), and \(t\) as in the statement.  Apply the coarea formula to the Lipschitz map \(z\mapsto\lVert z-x\rVert_2\) and the integrand \(f_P(z)\mathbf 1\{z\in\mathcal A_{t,P}\cap\mathcal X_P\}\).  Since the gradient of the distance has norm one away from the single Lebesgue-null point \(x\), for every \(r>0\),
\[
P\{X\in\mathcal A_{t,P}\cap B_2(x,r)\}
=\int_0^rQ_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds.
\]
For \(0<r\leq r_0\), uniform two-sided thickness supplies the lower bound \(c_{-}r^2\).  If the positive set of \(Q_{t,P,x}\) did not accumulate at zero, then \(Q_{t,P,x}=0\) almost everywhere on some interval \((0,r)\), contradicting this lower bound.

Apply coarea once more with the integrand \(\mu_{t,P}(z)f_P(z)\mathbf 1\{z\in\mathcal A_{t,P}\cap\mathcal X_P\}\).  Deterministic assignment and consistency imply that, on arm \(t\), \(Y=(1-t)Y(0)+tY(1)\) and its conditional mean given \(X=z\) is \(\mu_{t,P}(z)\).  Therefore the marginal density of the positive radius in arm \(t\) is \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)\), while the corresponding first-moment density is \(N_{t,P,x}(s)\).  The Radon--Nikodym characterization of conditional expectation consequently gives, for Lebesgue-almost every \(s>0\) with \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y\mid D_{P,x}=(2t-1)s]
=\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}.
\]
The required integrability follows from the conditional sub-Gaussian member property of either class and the bounded H\"older envelope.

Because \(q\geq1\), the H\"older-regression assumption gives
\(\lvert\mu_{t,P}(z)-\mu_{t,P}(x)\rvert\leq L\lVert z-x\rVert_2\).  When \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0\), the ratio \(N/Q\) is a probability-weighted average of \(\mu_{t,P}\) over points at distance \(s\), and hence
\[
\left|\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}-\mu_{t,P}(x)\right|\leq Ls.
\]
When \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)=0\), and also when \(s=0\), the canonical definition sets the value equal to \(\mu_{t,P}(x)\), so the same inequality holds, including every boundary case of the division.  Letting \(s\downarrow0\) separately for \(t=1\) and \(t=0\), and then using the definition of the causal target, yields
\[
\lim_{s\downarrow0}\{g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{1,P,x}(s)-g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{0,P,x}(s)\}
=\mu_{1,P}(x)-\mu_{0,P}(x)=\tau_P(x).
\]

statements.statement:
There are constants \(c_0,c_1>0\) and \(0<\alpha<1/8\), depending only on the law-class parameters and \(\delta\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), one can construct \(M_n\geq c_0a_n^{-1/q}\) centers on a trimmed straight boundary, separated by a constant multiple of \(a_n^{1/q}\), and a finite hypercube family of laws in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rect}}\cap\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}\).  The assignment interface is straight; the regressions are disjoint \(q\)-H\"older bump perturbations of affine baselines; every \(f_P\) is continuous and stays within the fixed density envelope; and the variance, tail, and arm-specific local-mass constants are common.  If two vertices differ only in the coordinate attached to a center \(x_j\), their target curves differ by at least \(c_1a_n\) at \(x_j\), both arm-specific radial mass densities at \(x_j\) agree at every radius, their arm-specific radial laws at \(x_j\) agree outside radii of order \(a_n\), and
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left(\mathbb Q_{n,P_\omega,x_j},\mathbb Q_{n,P_{\omega^{(j)}},x_j}\right)
 \leq\alpha\log M_n.
\]
The perturbations use \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{ang}}\), and the density envelope and arm-specific local-mass bounds hold uniformly over the whole hypercube.  If \(L>4\), the construction may be made on the canonical square, in which case the entire family also lies in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}\).
statements.proof_tex:
We verify the construction, including support, normalization, positivity, smoothness, moment, and boundary conditions.

Fix first the square \(S=[-1/2,1/2]^2\), the two half-square assignment regions, and
\[
 \mathcal B=\{(u-1/2,0):0\leq u\leq1\},
 \qquad \gamma(u)=(u-1/2,0).
\]
The base score density is one.  The chart is injective, has length and speed one, has all derivatives of order at least two equal to zero, and its image, being a closed convex segment, has infinite reach.  Hence every smooth-boundary condition holds for every \(\iota\geq1\) and every finite \(\rho_0\).  At an endpoint, each arm intersected with a ball of radius at most \(r_0\leq1/4\) contains a quarter disk.  The densities below are at least \(3/4\), so each such arm has probability at least \(3\pi r^2/16\), which is greater than \(c_-r^2\) because \(c_-\leq1/(16L)\).  The same lower bound away from the endpoints is immediate.  The compact-support, partition, length, and two-sided-thickness conditions are therefore uniform.

Choose a nonnegative radial \(C^\infty\) function \(\phi\), supported in the open unit disk, with \(\phi(0)=1\).  For fixed constants \(d,d_1>0\), put
\[
 \Delta=d a_n,
 \qquad w=(d_1\Delta)^{1/q}.
\]
Choose centers \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\) on \(\gamma([\delta,1-\delta])\), separated by at least \(3w\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), the disks \(B_2(x_j,w)\) are disjoint and lie in the interior of \(S\), and one-dimensional packing gives
\[
 M\geq c w^{-1}\geq c_0a_n^{-1/q}.
\]
Write \(\phi_j(z)=\phi((z-x_j)/w)\).  For \(0\leq k\leq q\),
\[
 \lVert D^k(\Delta\phi_j)\rVert_\infty
 \leq C_\phi\Delta w^{-k}.
\]
The right-hand side is at most \(C_\phi/d_1\) when \(k=q\), and, after \(n\) is sufficiently large, also when \(k<q\).  Since the supports are disjoint, the same bounds hold for every signed sum.  Taking \(d_1\) sufficiently large and then taking a fixed affine slope \(b>0\) sufficiently small places all regressions below in the prescribed isotropic \(q\)-H\"older ball.

For \(\omega\in\{0,1\}^M\), define
\[
 p_{0,\omega}(z)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 p_{1,\omega}(z)=\frac12+bz_1+Delta\sum_{j=1}^M\omega_j\phi_j(z).
\]
After decreasing \(b\) and \(d\), these functions take values in \([1/4,3/4]\).  Conditional on \(X=z\), take independent potential outcomes
\[
 Y(t)=B_t+\varepsilon_t,
 \qquad B_t\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_{t,\omega}(z)),
 \qquad \varepsilon_t\sim N(0,1).
\]
Use the deterministic assignment rule and consistency to define \(T\) and \(Y\).  Then \(\mu_{t,P_\omega}=p_{t,\omega}\) and
\[
 1\leq\sigma^2_{t,P_\omega}(z)
 =1+p_{t,\omega}(z)\{1-p_{t,\omega}(z)\}
 \leq\frac54,
\]
which lies in \([L^{-1},L]\).  Hoeffding's exponential bound for a centered Bernoulli variable and the Gaussian moment-generating identity give, for every real \(\lambda\),
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\exp\{\lambda(Y(t)-p_{t,\omega}(X))\}\mid X\right]
 \leq e^{\lambda^2/8}e^{\lambda^2/2}
 \leq e^{L^2\lambda^2/2}.
\]
Thus the variance and tail envelopes are common to the entire family.

It remains to hide the \(j\)-th regression bump in the radial experiment centered at \(x_j\).  Let \(\chi\) be continuous, with \(\chi(v)=0\) for \(v\leq1\) and \(\chi(v)=1\) for \(v\geq2\), and define
\[
 A_n(r)=-\frac{2\Delta\phi(r/w)}{br}
 \chi\!\left(\frac{br}{8\Delta}\right).
\]
There is no division at zero: the cutoff vanishes on a neighborhood of zero, and the displayed expression is defined to be zero there.  On its active region \(br\geq8\Delta\), \(|A_n(r)|\leq1/4\).  Smooth compact support of \(\phi\) makes the correction vanish at the outer edge.  Define
\[
 f_\omega(z)=1+\sum_{j=1}^M\omega_j A_n(\lVert z-x_j\rVert_2)
 \frac{z_1-(x_j)_1}{\lVert z-x_j\rVert_2}
 \mathbf 1\{z\in B_2(x_j,w)\},
\]
with each summand set to zero at its center.  Disjointness makes the formula unambiguous.  The angular correction integrates to zero on every full circle and each bump disk lies inside \(S\), so \(\int_S f_\omega=1\).  Moreover, \(f_\omega\) is continuous and belongs to \([3/4,5/4]\subseteq[L^{-1},L]\).

Compare adjacent vertices \(\omega\) and \(\omega^{(j)}\), oriented so that \(\omega_j=1\).  On either half-circle centered at \(x_j\), \(\int\cos\theta\,d\theta=0\).  Hence the two arm-specific radial mass densities agree at every radius.  On the treated upper half-circle, whenever \(br\geq16\Delta\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\int_0^\pi p_{1,\omega}(x_j+r e_\theta)
       \{1+A_n(r)\cos\theta\}\,d\theta
 -\int_0^\pi p_{1,\omega^{(j)}}(x_j+r e_\theta)\,d\theta\\
 &\qquad=\pi\Delta\phi(r/w)+\frac\pi2brA_n(r)=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
For the control arm the equality follows from the constant regression.  A mixture of Bernoulli variables is Bernoulli with success probability equal to the mixed success probability, and adding the common Gaussian noise is a common Markov kernel.  Therefore both complete arm-specific radial outcome laws agree outside \(r\leq16\Delta/b\), not merely their conditional means.

Within this exceptional radius, the common radial density is bounded by \(Cr\), all success probabilities lie in \([1/4,3/4]\), and the radially averaged success probabilities differ by at most \(C\Delta\).  From \(\log u\leq u-1\),
\[
 \operatorname{kl}(p,p')\leq\frac{(p-p')^2}{p'(1-p')},
\]
and relative entropy cannot increase after adding the common Gaussian channel.  Hence one compressed observation obeys
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P^{\mathrm{dist}}_{\omega,x_j},
 P^{\mathrm{dist}}_{\omega^{(j)},x_j})
 \leq C\int_0^{16\Delta/b}\Delta^2r\,dr
 \leq C'\Delta^4.
\]
Independence tensorizes relative entropy, so
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\mathbb Q_{n,P_\omega,x_j},
 \mathbb Q_{n,P_{\omega^{(j)}},x_j})
 \leq C' n\Delta^4=C'd^4\log n.
\]
Also \(\log M=(1/(4q)+o(1))\log n\).  Choosing \(d\) sufficiently small gives the displayed bound with a fixed \(\alpha<1/8\).  At \(x_j\), the adjacent target values differ by \(\Delta\phi_j(x_j)=d a_n\), so one may take \(c_1=d\).  The global density bounds and fixed half-square geometry give the common arm-specific local-mass bounds.  Taking independent observations now completes membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rect}}\cap\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}\).

For the canonical square \([-1,1]^2\), use \(\gamma(u)=(2u-1,0)\) and base density \(1/4\).  If \(L>4\), set \(\varepsilon_L=1-4/L>0\), replace the cutoff constant eight by \(C_L\geq4/\varepsilon_L\), and multiply the preceding relative perturbation by the base density.  Choose \(d_1\) large enough that the cancellation region lies inside every bump, including when \(q=1\), and then choose \(d/b\) small enough that all disks remain away from the trimmed endpoints.  The relative density perturbation is at most \(\varepsilon_L/2\), whence
\[
 L^{-1}\leq\frac14(1-\varepsilon_L/2)
 \leq f_\omega(z)
 \leq\frac14(1+\varepsilon_L/2)\leq L.
\]
All cancellation and entropy calculations change only by constants depending on \(L\), proving the straight-class clause.  When \(L=4\), normalization and the lower envelope on a square of area four force \(f_P\equiv1/4\), so the strict-slack clause is correctly restricted to \(L>4\).
statements.justification: This explicit compressed-experiment construction converts angular-density confounding into the logarithmic uniform lower bound even under a perfectly smooth interface and smooth outcome regressions.
statements.gap: The published pointwise converse does not distribute continuous angular-density perturbations over separated trimmed-boundary centers with a logarithmic divergence budget.
statements.consumer: The rectifiable, smooth, and strict-slack straight-class distance converses use this family together with the coordinatewise overlap argument.

statements.statement: For every \(q\geq1\), there exist constants \(0<c_{\mathrm{rect}}\leq C_{\mathrm{rect}}<\infty\), depending only on \(q,L,c_{-},r_0\), such that \[c_{\mathrm{rect}}\leq\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_n^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}})}{a_n}\leq\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_n^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}})}{a_n}\leq C_{\mathrm{rect}}.\] The upper inequality is attained by the fixed degree-zero triangular-kernel estimator \(\widehat{\tau}^{\mathrm{LC}}_{n,h}\) with \(h\asymp a_n\). The lower inequality is supplied by the separated compressed-experiment family in \(\mathrm{lem:angular\text{-}density\text{-}packing}\). This theorem concerns the explicitly defined primitive two-sided-thickness class and asserts no inclusion in, or same-class tightening of, the nonparametric class in Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu, Theorem 6.
statements.justification: The theorem gives the sharp logarithm-bearing uniform frontier for the primitive rectifiable coordinatewise-distance experiment.
statements.gap: The published lower bound is pointwise in its packing architecture.  This theorem obtains the logarithmic factor on a separately defined two-sided-thickness class and makes no class-inclusion claim.
statements.consumer: Distance-based boundary analyses receive a rate-sharp bandwidth and worst-case uniform error guarantee under an inspectable arm-mass condition.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(h=h_n\asymp a_n\).  We first prove the upper bound with the single estimator specified in the statement.  For \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), put
\[
 W_{i,t,x}=\mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}K_\triangle(D_{P,x,i}/h),
 \qquad A_{t,x}=\sum_{i=1}^nW_{i,t,x}.
\]
Because \(K_\triangle\) is symmetric, the arm is recovered from the sign of \(D_{P,x,i}\) except on the probability-zero event \(D_{P,x,i}=0\).  Thus the estimator is a measurable function of \(U_{n,P}(x)\) at every \(x\), and \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{LC}}_{n,h}\in\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\).

On arm \(t\), let \(\varepsilon_{i,t}=Y_i-\mu_{t,P}(X_i)\).  Whenever \(A_{t,x}>0\), algebra gives
\[
 \widehat\mu_{t,h}(x)-\mu_{t,P}(x)
 =\frac{\sum_iW_{i,t,x}\varepsilon_{i,t}}{A_{t,x}}
 +\frac{\sum_iW_{i,t,x}\{\mu_{t,P}(X_i)-\mu_{t,P}(x)\}}{A_{t,x}}.
\]
Every nonzero weight has \(\lVert X_i-x\rVert_2\leq h\).  Since \(q\geq1\), the H\"older condition bounds the second term by \(Lh\).  The stability and upper-mass lemmas give, uniformly in \(P,t,x\),
\[
 \kappa_0nh^2\leq\mathbb E_PA_{t,x}\leq\pi Lnh^2.
\]
These are the positivity and scale bounds used below.

Take a maximal \(n^{-3}\)-net of \(\mathcal B_P\).  Since the boundary lies in \([-L,L]^2\), the net has at most \(C_Ln^6\) points.  For a fixed net point, the summands in \(A_{t,x}\) lie in \([0,1]\) and have total variance at most \(\mathbb E_PA_{t,x}\).  Exponential Markov applied to the elementary bounded-variable moment-generating bound therefore yields
\[
 P\{|A_{t,x}-\mathbb E_PA_{t,x}|>u\}
 \leq2\exp\!\left\{-\frac{u^2}{2(\mathbb E_PA_{t,x}+u/3)}\right\}.
\]
A union bound, followed by the one-Lipschitz property of \(K_\triangle\), yields an event \(E_n\) such that \(\sup_PP(E_n^c)\leq n^{-4}\) and
\[
 \inf_{t,x}A_{t,x}\geq\frac{\kappa_0}{2}nh^2,
 \qquad \sup_{t,x}A_{t,x}\leq Cnh^2.
\]
Indeed, moving a center by \(n^{-3}\) changes \(A_{t,x}\) by at most \(n^{-2}/h=o(nh^2)\), and \(nh^2/\log n\to\infty\).

Conditionally on \(X_{1:n}\), independence and the conditional sub-Gaussian assumption give
\[
 \Pr_P\!\left(\left.\left|\sum_iW_{i,t,x}\varepsilon_{i,t}\right|>u\,\right|X_{1:n}\right)
 \leq2\exp\!\left\{-\frac{u^2}{2L^2\sum_iW_{i,t,x}^2}\right\}
 \leq2\exp\!\left\{-\frac{u^2}{2L^2A_{t,x}}\right\}.
\]
Union over the net, integration of this tail, and the denominator bounds on \(E_n\) give
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rect}}}
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{t,x}\frac{|\sum_iW_{i,t,x}\varepsilon_{i,t}|}{A_{t,x}}
 \mathbf1_{E_n}\right]
 \leq C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^2}}+o(a_n).
\]
For the extension off the net, the expected numerator oscillation is at most
\(n^{-3}h^{-1}\mathbb E_P\sum_i|\varepsilon_{i,t}|=O(n^{-2}/h)\), which is negligible after division by \(nh^2\).  The H\"older ball bounds the regressions uniformly, and conditional sub-Gaussianity implies
\(\sup_P\mathbb E_P\max_{i\leq n}|Y_i|^2=O(\log n)\).  On \(E_n^c\), every nonempty-denominator local average is bounded by \(\max_i|Y_i|\); Cauchy--Schwarz makes its expected contribution \(o(a_n)\).  A zero denominator lies in \(E_n^c\) and is covered by the estimator's zero convention.  Summing the two arms proves
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rect}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B_P}
 |\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{LC}}_{n,h}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \leq C\left\{h+\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^2}}\right\}.
\]
Balancing gives \(h\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/4}=a_n\), proving the upper limsup.

For the converse, apply the angular-density packing with, say, the fixed trim \(\delta=1/4\).  It gives \(M=M_n\) disjoint centers and adjacent target separation \(\Delta=c_1a_n\).  Poissonize the sample at mean \(2n\).  Conditional on the hypercube bits, the marked observations in the disjoint bump disks are independent Poisson processes \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_M\); the outside process \(Z_0\) is bit-independent.  These point-process spaces are standard Borel.  Decoder \(j\)'s observations from its own disk form a measurable signed-distance compression \(S_j\) of \(Z_j\), while revealing \(Z_{-j}\) and \(Z_0\) only makes decoding easier.  Equality of adjacent radial mass laws and Poisson relative-entropy tensorization give
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})
 \leq2\alpha\log M=:\kappa\log M,
 \qquad \kappa<1.
\]
The coordinatewise-overlap direct-product lemma therefore yields, under the uniform product prior,
\[
 \Pr\{\widehat\omega_j\neq\omega_j\text{ for at least one }j\}
 \geq\frac12-o(1).
\]
At \(x_j\), thresholding \(\widehat\tau_n(x_j)\) at the midpoint of the two possible target values recovers bit \(j\) whenever the sup-norm error is below \(\Delta/2\).  Thus the Poissonized Bayes expected sup-norm loss is at least
\((\Delta/2)(1/2-o(1))\).

To return to a fixed sample, on the event that a Poisson count \(N\) of mean \(2n\) is at least \(n\), select \(n\) observations uniformly and apply any fixed-\(n\) rule.  The selected observations have law \(P^{\otimes n}\), and \(P(N<n)\leq e^{-cn}\).  On the complement use the zero curve.  The target is uniformly bounded by the H\"older envelope, so the de-Poissonization remainder is \(o(\Delta)\).  Hence every fixed-\(n\) rule has worst-law risk at least \(ca_n\), and
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_n^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rect}})}{a_n}>0.
\]
Combining the two bounds proves the theorem.  The causal target remains \(\tau_P\); the canonical radial regression provides its observed-data limit and does not define the causal effect.

statements.statement: Fix \(\delta\in(0,1/2)\). For every \(q\geq1\) and \(\iota\geq1\), there exist constants \(0<c_{\mathrm{sm},\delta}\leq C_{\mathrm{sm},\delta}<\infty\), depending only on \(q,\iota,L,c_{-},r_0,\rho_0,\delta\), such that \[c_{\mathrm{sm},\delta}\leq\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}})}{a_n}\leq\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}})}{a_n}\leq C_{\mathrm{sm},\delta}.\] The upper inequality is attained by \(\widehat{\tau}^{\mathrm{LC}}_{n,h}\) with \(h\asymp a_n\) and uses only the first-order continuity implied by \(q\geq1\), arm-specific local mass, and the fixed triangular kernel. The lower inequality is attained by the straight-interface, compact-support hard family in the narrowed \(\mathrm{lem:angular\text{-}density\text{-}packing}\); its regressions are disjoint \(q\)-H\"older bump perturbations of affine baselines, and its bounded continuous score densities have no common modulus.
statements.proof_tex:
The upper bound uses the same explicit local-constant estimator, now over \(x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\).  For either arm, the stability lemma gives
\(\mathbb E_PA_{t,x}\geq\kappa_0nh^2\), the upper-mass lemma gives \(\mathbb E_PA_{t,x}\leq\pi Lnh^2\), and \(q\geq1\) gives bias at most \(Lh\).  A maximal \(n^{-3}\)-net has polynomial cardinality because the trimmed boundary lies in \([-L,L]^2\); the smooth-boundary length lemma alternatively gives a one-dimensional cover.  The bounded-summand exponential inequality and the conditional sub-Gaussian calculation used for the rectifiable class, followed by the one-Lipschitz kernel extension, yield an event of complement probability at most \(n^{-4}\) on which both empirical denominators are between fixed multiples of \(nh^2\), and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 |\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{LC}}_{n,h}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \leq C\left\{h+\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^2}}\right\}.
\]
On the exceptional event, a nonempty-denominator local average is bounded by \(\max_i|Y_i|\), whose squared expectation is \(O(\log n)\); the zero-denominator convention handles the remaining boundary case.  Thus the exceptional contribution is negligible.  Taking \(h\asymp a_n\) proves the upper limsup with a single distance-only estimator.

For the lower bound, use the unit-square version of the angular-density packing.  Its interface is a straight \(C^\infty\) embedded segment, its chart has speed one and vanishing higher derivatives, and the segment has infinite reach.  Its centers lie in \(\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\), and the packing proof verifies the density, variance, tail, H\"older, and two-sided-mass envelopes uniformly.  Consequently every vertex belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}\) for every \(\iota\geq1\).

Poissonizing at mean \(2n\) makes the marked observations in the disjoint disks conditionally independent standard-Borel point processes, with a bit-independent outside process.  At center \(x_j\), the own-disk signed-radius process is the compression \(S_j\), while all other processes may be revealed.  The packing entropy bound gives
\(\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})\leq2\alpha\log M\) with \(2\alpha<1\).  The coordinatewise-overlap direct-product lemma then makes the probability of at least one bit error at least \(1/2-o(1)\).  Adjacent target values are separated by \(c_1a_n\), so midpoint thresholding turns a sup-norm error smaller than half this amount into exact recovery.  Uniformly subsampling \(n\) points when the Poisson count of mean \(2n\) exceeds \(n\), whose complement has exponentially small probability, proves
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \frac{R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}})}{a_n}>0.
\]
Together with the upper bound this proves the theorem.  The hard regressions are disjoint \(q\)-H\"older bump perturbations of affine baselines; smooth boundary geometry by itself does not remove their angular-density confounding.
statements.justification: The theorem isolates a genuine information bottleneck: smooth assignment geometry alone cannot accelerate coordinatewise distance estimation uniformly over densities lacking a shared angular regularity modulus.
statements.gap: The published smooth-bias calculation is fixed-law and does not provide a class-uniform higher-order constant under only bounded continuity of the score density.
statements.consumer: Analysts with a smooth assignment map learn when the stable degree-zero distance procedure is the honest uniform default.

statements.statement:
Fix \(\delta\in(0,1/2)\).  On the nonempty canonical class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}\),
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})\asymp s_{n,q}.
\]
If \(L>4\), then
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})\asymp a_n,
\]
and the distance lower bound is direct from the canonical-square version of the narrowed \(\mathrm{lem:angular\text{-}density\text{-}packing}\).  If \(L=4\), then the density envelope and the fixed square support force \(f_P\equiv1/4\), and
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})\asymp s_{n,q}.
\]
Consequently the distance and location exponents are strictly separated for \(q>1\) when \(L>4\), while they coincide when \(q=1\) and also throughout the no-density-slack boundary case \(L=4\).
statements.proof_tex:
We first verify nonemptiness.  Take the uniform score density \(1/4\) on \([-1,1]^2\), the prescribed half-square assignment regions, \(\gamma_P(u)=(2u-1,0)\), constant regressions in \((1/4,3/4)\), and Bernoulli potential outcomes with independent standard Gaussian noise.  The chart has speed two and vanishing derivatives of order at least two, and its image, a closed convex segment, has infinite reach.  A boundary ball contains in each arm at least a quarter disk, so its arm mass is at least \(\pi r^2/16\geq c_-r^2\).  The support, density, assignment, H\"older, variance, and sub-Gaussian conditions all hold.

For the full-location upper bound, choose a fixed compactly supported Lipschitz bivariate kernel positive on the unit disk.  On each arm, fit a total-degree-\((q-1)\) local polynomial in \((X_i-x)/h\), use its intercept only when the smallest eigenvalue of the scaled empirical Gram matrix exceeds a fixed positive threshold, and use zero otherwise; subtract the two arm intercepts.  This is an explicit jointly measurable function of the full sample and known geometry, hence belongs to \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\).  Endpoint trimming leaves a fixed distance from the vertical sides.  For all sufficiently small \(h\), each population Gram quadratic form is the integral of the square of a polynomial against a density at least \(L^{-1}\) on a fixed half-disk.  A nonzero polynomial cannot vanish on that open set, so compactness of the unit sphere in the fixed-dimensional coefficient space gives a uniform strictly positive minimum eigenvalue.  This is the required rank and inverse condition.

Taylor's formula through degree \(q-1\) gives bias at most \(Ch^q\).  Entrywise exponential bounds for the bounded Gram summands, and conditional sub-Gaussian exponential bounds for the outcome sums, on a polynomial boundary net imply
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 |\widetilde\tau_{n,h}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \leq C\left\{h^q+\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^2}}\right\}.
\]
The kernel's Lipschitz property extends the bounds off the net.  The eigenvalue cutoff makes the estimator zero on the exceptional event, whose probability is polynomially small, so no uncontrolled inverse occurs.  Taking \(h\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(2q+2)}\) proves the upper bound \(Cs_{n,q}\).

For the matching converse, retain the uniform score density and place \(M\asymp h^{-1}\) disjoint smooth bivariate regression bumps of width \(h\) and height \(c h^q\) at trimmed boundary centers.  Use the same Gaussian-noised Bernoulli outcomes.  For sufficiently small fixed \(c\), every alternative belongs to the straight class and adjacent target curves are separated by \(c h^q\).  Since a bump has area \(O(h^2)\), the Bernoulli relative-entropy inequality and data processing through the Gaussian channel give
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_j^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 \leq Cn(h^q)^2h^2=Cnh^{2q+2}.
\]
At \(h\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(2q+2)}\), reduce \(c\) so this is at most \(\alpha\log M\) with \(\alpha<1\).  If \(J\) is uniform on the \(M\) alternatives and \(Z=O_{1:n}\), convexity of relative entropy gives
\[
 I(J;Z)\leq M^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^M
 \operatorname{KL}(P_j^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 \leq\alpha\log M.
\]
For any decoder with error probability \(p_e\), writing the conditional entropy according to the error indicator gives
\(H(J\mid Z)\leq\log2+p_e\log M\), and hence
\(I(J;Z)\geq(1-p_e)\log M-\log2\).  Thus \(p_e\) stays bounded away from zero.  Sup-norm accuracy below half the bump height would identify \(J\), so
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})
 \geq c s_{n,q}.
\]
This proves the full-location equivalence.

Suppose next that \(L>4\).  The distance local-constant calculation, with denominator order \(nh^2\), first-order bias \(Ch\), and stochastic term \(C\sqrt{\log n/(nh^2)}\), gives the upper bound \(Ca_n\).  The canonical-square angular family is contained in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}\) because the strict density-envelope slack permits its nonzero relative angular perturbations.  In the mean-\(2n\) Poisson experiment, its disjoint local channels satisfy the premises of the coordinatewise-overlap direct-product lemma with relative entropy at most \(2\alpha\log M\), and \(2\alpha<1\).  Midpoint thresholding followed by the exponentially accurate fixed-sample subsampling argument therefore gives the matching lower bound \(ca_n\).

Finally suppose \(L=4\).  The square has area four and \(f_P\geq1/4\), so
\[
 1=\int_{[-1,1]^2}f_P(z)\,dz\geq1.
\]
Equality forces \(f_P=1/4\) almost everywhere, and continuity makes the equality pointwise.  For a trimmed boundary point and sufficiently small \(s\), each arm-specific half-circle lies inside the square, and therefore
\[
 Q_{t,P,x}(s)=\frac\pi4s.
\]
Taylor's formula for the bivariate \(q\)-H\"older regression, integrated over that half-circle, gives uniformly bounded coefficients with
\[
 \left|g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)-\mu_{t,P}(x)
 -\sum_{k=1}^{q-1}b_{t,k,P}(x)s^k\right|\leq Cs^q.
\]
Fit a degree-\((q-1)\) one-sided local polynomial in the signed radius and apply the same fixed eigenvalue cutoff.  Its limiting Gram quadratic form integrates the square of a nonzero polynomial against \(uK_\triangle(u)\,du\) on \((0,1)\), so it is uniformly positive definite.  The estimator consequently has risk
\[
 C\left\{h^q+\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^2}}\right\},
\]
and balancing gives \(Cs_{n,q}\).  Every distance-only rule can be implemented from the full scores and known geometry, so \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\) is informationally no larger than \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\); the full-location lower bound thus gives the distance lower bound \(cs_{n,q}\).  Since \(q/(2q+2)>1/4\) exactly when \(q>1\), all asserted separation and coincidence cases follow.
statements.justification: Holding geometry and the causal target fixed reveals the statistical price of releasing only one distance coordinate, and also identifies the no-density-slack exception.
statements.gap: The full-regressor benchmark and location-based boundary theory do not pair their rate with a direct distance-only angular-confounding converse on the identical straight class.
statements.consumer: A data steward can determine whether a distance-only release loses an exponent: it does for \(q>1\) only when \(L>4\), and it does not when \(L=4\).

statements.statement:
There is no density-only weakest regularity threshold for the faster distance frontier.  The operational threshold is a joint coarea remainder of the density, regression, and boundary geometry.  Precisely, fix an integer \(m\) with \(1\leq m\leq\min\{q,\iota\}\), and let \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}\) be any subclass for which there are constants \(A<\infty\), \(r_*>0\), and \(0<\underline c\leq\overline c<\infty\) such that, for every \(P\in\mathcal C\), \(x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<s\leq r_*\),
\[
 \underline c s\leq Q_{t,P,x}(s)\leq\overline c s,
 \qquad
 \left|\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}-\mu_{t,P}(x)-\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}b_{t,k,P}(x)s^k\right|\leq As^m,
\]
for coefficient functions uniformly bounded over \(P,t,x,k\).  Then the explicit coordinatewise degree-\((m-1)\) local-polynomial estimator with bandwidth \(h\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(2m+2)}\) obeys
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal C)\leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
If \(\mathcal C\) contains the uniform-design, straight-interface H\"older bump submodel of order \(m\), the reverse inequality holds and the displayed rate is exact.  In contrast, any class containing the shrinking angular-imbalance family generated by \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{ang}}\) has lower frontier \(ca_n\).  Thus \(m=1\) is first-order saturation and every \(m\geq2\) gives a faster geometry-sensitive frontier.  A condition on \(f_P\) alone is neither necessary nor sufficient for the order: the normalized product integrals \(N/Q\), rather than the density in isolation, are the minimal operational objects.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(m\) and \(\mathcal C\) as in the statement.  For \(x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\), put \(S_{P,x}=|D_{P,x}|\) and \(v_m(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^{m-1})^\top\).  For \(0<h\leq r_*\), define
\[
 \widehat G_{t,x}(h)=\frac1{nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf1\{T_i=t\}
 K_\triangle(S_{P,x,i}/h)v_m(S_{P,x,i}/h)v_m(S_{P,x,i}/h)^\top
\]
and
\[
 \widehat r_{t,x}(h)=\frac1{nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf1\{T_i=t\}
 K_\triangle(S_{P,x,i}/h)v_m(S_{P,x,i}/h)Y_i.
\]
Let
\[
 G_m=\int_0^1uK_\triangle(u)v_m(u)v_m(u)^\top\,du,
 \qquad \lambda_* =\underline c\,\lambda_{\min}(G_m)>0.
\]
Define the stabilized intercept by
\[
 \widehat\mu^{(m)}_{t,h}(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 e_1^\top\widehat G_{t,x}(h)^{-1}\widehat r_{t,x}(h),
 &\lambda_{\min}(\widehat G_{t,x}(h))\geq\lambda_*/2,\\
 0,&\text{otherwise},
 \end{cases}
\]
and set \(\widehat\tau^{(m)}_{n,h}=\widehat\mu^{(m)}_{1,h}-\widehat\mu^{(m)}_{0,h}\).  The arm is recovered from the sign of \(D_{P,x}\) away from its probability-zero origin, so this is an explicit measurable function of \(U_{n,P}(x)\) and belongs to \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\).  The eigenvalue cutoff states every inverse and boundary convention explicitly.

Coarea and the radial mass bounds give
\[
 \mathbb E_P\widehat G_{t,x}(h)
 =\int_0^1K_\triangle(u)v_m(u)v_m(u)^\top
 \frac{Q_{t,P,x}(hu)}h\,du.
\]
Thus, for every \(a\in\mathbb R^m\),
\[
 \underline c\int_0^1uK_\triangle(u)\{a^\top v_m(u)\}^2du
 \leq a^\top\mathbb E_P\widehat G_{t,x}(h)a
 \leq\overline c\int_0^1uK_\triangle(u)\{a^\top v_m(u)\}^2du.
\]
A nonzero polynomial cannot vanish on an interval of positive measure.  Hence \(G_m\) is positive definite; since \(m\) is fixed, the displayed inequalities give uniform population rank and inverse bounds.

Write
\[
 g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)
 =\mu_{t,P}(x)+\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}b_{t,k,P}(x)s^k+R_{t,P,x}(s),
 \qquad |R_{t,P,x}(s)|\leq As^m.
\]
On the event that the eigenvalue cutoff passes, the empirical normal equations reproduce the polynomial exactly.  The scaled coefficient vector is
\((\mu_{t,P}(x),h b_{t,1,P}(x),\ldots,h^{m-1}b_{t,m-1,P}(x))^\top\).  Since \(|R_{t,P,x}(S)|\leq Ah^m\) on the kernel support, the uniform inverse bound and the bounded empirical kernel moments give an intercept remainder at most \(Ch^m\).

For completeness, the stochastic scale follows directly from the primitive tails.  Conditional on \(T=t\) and \(S_{P,x}=s\),
\[
 Y-g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)
 =\{Y-\mu_{t,P}(X)\}
 +\{\mu_{t,P}(X)-g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)\}.
\]
The first term satisfies the stated conditional sub-Gaussian bound.  The second is conditionally centered and bounded by the H\"older envelope; applying the bounded centered moment-generating inequality after conditioning on \(S_{P,x}\) shows that their sum is conditionally sub-Gaussian with a constant depending only on \(L\).

Take a maximal \(n^{-3}\)-net of the trimmed boundary.  The smooth-boundary length lemma, or the ambient square bound, gives polynomial cardinality.  Each Gram entry, after the \(h^{-2}\) scaling, is bounded by \(Ch^{-2}\), while its second moment is bounded by \(Ch^{-2}\) because \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)\leq\overline c s\).  Exponential Markov applied entrywise and a union bound therefore give
\[
 \sup_{P,t,x}\left\|\widehat G_{t,x}(h)-
 \mathbb E_P\widehat G_{t,x}(h)\right\|
 =O_P\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^2}}
ight)
\]
with complement probability at most \(n^{-4}\).  The kernel-polynomial weight is Lipschitz after extension by zero outside \([0,1]\); its oscillation between a point and its net representative is \(O(n^{-3}h^{-3})\), which is negligible at the bandwidth below.  Weyl's inequality then makes the cutoff pass uniformly because \(nh^2/\log n\to\infty\).

At a net point, conditionally on the signed radii, the coefficient of each centered outcome in the stabilized intercept is at most \(C/(nh^2)\), and the sum of squared coefficients is at most \(C/(nh^2)\).  The preceding conditional sub-Gaussian bound therefore gives
\[
 P\!\left\{|\widehat\mu^{(m)}_{t,h}(x)
 -\mathbb E[\widehat\mu^{(m)}_{t,h}(x)\mid D_{P,x,1:n}]|>u\right\}
 \leq2e^{-cnh^2u^2}
\]
on the good Gram event.  A union bound over the net and tail integration produce \(C\sqrt{\log n/(nh^2)}\).  To extend off the net, work with the original outcome vector \(\widehat r_{t,x}\): its kernel weights are Lipschitz in \(x\), and conditional sub-Gaussianity gives \(\mathbb E\max_i|Y_i|^2=O(\log n)\).  The \(n^{-3}\)-mesh error is therefore negligible.  The H\"older condition similarly controls the target's mesh oscillation.  On the exceptional Gram event the stabilized estimator is zero and the target is uniformly bounded, so its expected contribution is negligible.  Consequently
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal C}\mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 |\widehat\tau^{(m)}_{n,h}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \leq C\left\{h^m+\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^2}}\right\}.
\]
Balancing the terms gives
\[
 h\asymp\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(2m+2)},
 \qquad
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal C)
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]

For the conditional converse, use the uniform-design straight-interface submodel whose containment in \(\mathcal C\) is the theorem's explicit premise.  Place \(M\asymp h^{-1}\) disjoint smooth bivariate regression bumps of width \(h\) and height \(c h^m\) at trimmed centers, and use Gaussian-noised Bernoulli outcomes.  The premise supplies submodel membership; directly, adjacent target values differ by \(c h^m\), while one bump has score mass \(O(h^2)\).  The Bernoulli relative-entropy inequality and data processing give
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_j^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 \leq Cn h^{2m+2}.
\]
At the displayed bandwidth, choose the fixed amplitude small enough that this is at most \(\alpha\log M\), with \(\alpha<1\).  For a uniform bump index \(J\),
\[
 I(J;O_{1:n})\leq M^{-1}\sum_j
 \operatorname{KL}(P_j^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n}),
 \qquad
 I(J;O_{1:n})\geq(1-p_e)\log M-\log2.
\]
The second inequality follows by decomposing \(H(J\mid O_{1:n})\) according to the decoding-error indicator.  Thus every decoder errs with probability bounded away from zero.  Sup-norm accuracy below half the bump height would decode the center, proving the matching lower bound \(ch^m\).

If a class contains the shrinking angular-imbalance family, its adjacent separation is \(c a_n\).  In the mean-\(2n\) Poisson experiment, disjoint local point processes are conditionally independent standard-Borel channels and the outside process is bit-independent.  The packing entropy slack and the coordinatewise-overlap direct-product lemma give probability at least \(1/2-o(1)\) of some bit error, even after all cross-center observations are revealed.  Thresholding and fixed-sample subsampling yield the lower frontier \(ca_n\).  At \(m=1\), the upper rate equals \(a_n\), while for \(m\geq2\), \(m/(2m+2)>1/4\).

Finally, the normalized coarea product, rather than density smoothness in isolation, is the object used in every bias calculation.  Bounded continuity alone is not sufficient: it permits the shrinking angular-imbalance family and its \(a_n\) lower bound.  Nor is density differentiability necessary for the upper order: with a bounded continuous positive but nondifferentiable density and a regression locally constant on the relevant circles, one has \(N_{t,P,x}(s)/Q_{t,P,x}(s)=\mu_{t,P}(x)\) exactly.  More generally, the same continuous radial-angular density can be paired either with such a constant regression or, for \(m\geq2\), with an affine regression whose angular product moment has a nonpolynomial remainder of order below \(m\).  Thus no necessary-and-sufficient threshold stated solely in terms of \(f_P\) can characterize the faster order; the joint \(N/Q\) remainder is the operational condition.  Throughout, \(\tau_P\) is the causal curve, while \(N/Q\) is its identifying radial regression and is not a redefinition of the causal target.

statements.statement:
Let all spaces carrying \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_M,S_1,\ldots,S_M\) be standard Borel.  Let \(\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M\) be independent uniform binary variables.  Conditionally on them, let \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_M\) be independent, with the law of \(Z_j\) depending only on \(\Omega_j\) for \(1\leq j\leq M\), and with the law of \(Z_0\) independent of \((\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M)\).  Suppose decoder \(j\) is measurable with respect to \((S_j,Z_{-j},Z_0)\), where \(S_j\) is a measurable compression of \(Z_j\), and write \(Q_{j,b}=\mathcal L(S_j\mid\Omega_j=b)\) and \(\rho_j=1-\lVert Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\).  Then every such decentralized decoder obeys
\[
 \Pr\{\widehat\Omega_j=\Omega_j\text{ for every }j\}
 \leq\frac12\left\{1+\prod_{j=1}^M(1-\rho_j)\right\}.
\]
In particular, if \(\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})\leq\kappa\log M\) for all \(j\) and a fixed \(\kappa<1\), then the probability of at least one decoding error is at least \(1/2-o(1)\).
statements.proof_tex:
For each \(j\), dominate \(Q_{j,0}\) and \(Q_{j,1}\) by their sum and write their densities as \(q_{j,0}\) and \(q_{j,1}\).  The common subprobability measure has density \(q_{j,0}\wedge q_{j,1}\) and mass
\[
 \rho_j=\int(q_{j,0}\wedge q_{j,1})
 =1-\lVert Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\]
Generate the binary compressed experiment by first drawing an ambiguity indicator \(A_j\), independent of \(\Omega_j\), with \(\Pr(A_j=1)=\rho_j\).  On \(A_j=1\), draw \(S_j\) from the normalized common submeasure, independently of \(\Omega_j\); on \(A_j=0\), draw it from the normalized residual measure corresponding to \(\Omega_j\).  Zero-mass cases may be assigned arbitrary kernels because their indicators then have probability zero.  Use independent indicators and seeds across \(j\).  Because all observation spaces are standard Borel, a regular conditional kernel for \(Z_j\) given \((S_j,\Omega_j)\) exists; applying it reconstructs the original local experiment.  Independently draw the bit-independent ancillary \(Z_0\) from its fixed law.  The conditional product premise shows that this coupling preserves the joint law of the stated experiment.

Fix the ambiguity indicators, all non-bit seeds, and the bits outside the ambiguous coordinate set \(A=\{j:A_j=1\}\).  If \(A\neq\varnothing\), consider the configurations of \((\Omega_j:j\in A)\) on which every decoder is correct.  Two configurations that differ only at coordinate \(j\in A\) cannot both succeed: decoder \(j\) sees the same \(S_j\), the same \(Z_{-j}\), and the same \(Z_0\) at the two endpoints, so its output is unchanged while the correct bit is reversed.  The successful configurations therefore form an independent set in the \(|A|\)-dimensional hypercube.  Pairing vertices along any coordinate shows that this set has at most \(2^{|A|-1}\) elements.  The ambiguous bits remain uniform, so conditional exact-success probability is at most \(1/2\).  If \(A=\varnothing\), it is at most one.  Averaging proves
\[
 \Pr\{\widehat\Omega_j=\Omega_j\text{ for every }j\}
 \leq\Pr(A=\varnothing)+\frac12\Pr(A\neq\varnothing)
 =\frac12\left\{1+\prod_{j=1}^M(1-\rho_j)\right\}.
\]

For the relative-entropy consequence, define the Hellinger affinity \(H_j=\int\sqrt{q_{j,0}q_{j,1}}\).  Jensen's inequality under \(Q_{j,0}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})\geq-2\log H_j.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \lVert Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \leq\sqrt{1-H_j^2}
 \leq\sqrt{1-e^{-\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})}}.
\]
Since \(1-\sqrt{1-u}\geq u/2\) for \(0\leq u\leq1\),
\[
 \rho_j\geq\frac12e^{-\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})}
 \geq\frac12M^{-\kappa}.
\]
Therefore \(\prod_j(1-\rho_j)\leq\exp\{-M^{1-\kappa}/2\}=o(1)\), and the preceding exact-success bound implies an any-error probability at least \(1/2-o(1)\).

sampling_model.design: A boundary discontinuity design with a known binary assignment partition of a compact bivariate score support.
sampling_model.overlap: Each arm has probability mass at least \(c_{-}r^2\) in every boundary ball of radius \(r\) for \(0<r\leq r_0\); \(f_P\leq L\) yields the derived upper estimate \(\pi Lr^2\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The score density is bounded and continuous but has no class-uniform derivative or continuity modulus. Exact-distance regressions use the canonical coarea ratio on positive-denominator radii and the H\"older regression representative on zero-denominator radii. Both distance upper bounds use the fixed triangular kernel and degree zero; the comparison experiment permits estimators to use full score locations jointly.

tldr: The coordinatewise distance experiment has a sharp first-order uniform frontier even when the assignment boundary and outcome regressions are arbitrarily smooth. On the primitive rectifiable class with an inspectable arm-specific two-sided design-thickness condition, \(R_n^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}})\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/4}\). The same rate holds on the endpoint-trimmed smooth class because bounded continuous score densities have no common angular regularity modulus; a straight-boundary angular-density packing with affine regressions supplies the converse. On the identical straight geometry, full score locations recover \((\log n/n)^{q/(2q+2)}\), strictly faster for \(q>1\). A central open question asks which primitive density or angular-balance regularity produces a transition to a faster distance-only frontier.

project_justification.gap: Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu, Theorem 6, gives an \(n^{-1/4}\) pointwise-style lower bound over its stated nonparametric class, while the following discussion predicts that uniform estimation carries a logarithmic factor. Their Theorem 3(ii) is a fixed-law interior smooth-bias result and does not determine a class-uniform minimax rate when continuous score densities have no common modulus.
project_justification.niche: The coordinatewise distance release discards angular locations. A primitive two-sided design-thickness condition stabilizes local estimation and supplies separated boundary neighborhoods, while unrestricted shrinking-scale angular imbalance can keep the induced radial regression only first-order regular even on a straight boundary.
project_justification.fill: The rectifiable theorem establishes the predicted logarithmic phenomenon on its own transparent primitive class. The smooth saturation theorem shows that geometry alone does not improve that frontier, and the straight-class comparison isolates the lost information by proving the faster Stone exponent for the full-location experiment.

related_work: CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance is the anchor. Its Theorem 1 supplies distance-based BATEC identification as background; the present supporting coarea lemma fixes a canonical exact-distance conditional representative, including its values on zero-denominator radii, for the proposal's primitive classes. Its Theorem 6 proves an \(n^{-1/4}\) lower bound over a class defined by independent sampling, bounded continuous density on compact support, a rectifiable support boundary, H\"older regression, and bounded continuous variance; Assumption 2(iv)'s Gram condition is not a premise of that theorem. The discussion after Theorem 6 conjectures that the missing logarithm reflects the pointwise lower-bound construction. The rectifiable result here establishes that logarithmic phenomenon on a separately defined primitive two-sided-thickness class, with no asserted inclusion or transfer. Theorem 3(ii) of the same paper is a fixed-law interior two-intersection bias statement; its supplemental angular-integral differentiation does not supply a common higher-order bias constant over the present bounded continuous density envelope, and the saturation theorem does not challenge the published fixed-law result. CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Location supplies the full-location benchmark experiment, while CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Survey documents the applied prevalence of location- and distance-based boundary analyses. Stone1982OptimalGlobal supplies the classical bivariate sup-norm exponent recovered by the full-location risk on the straight subclass. ChenChristensen2018SupNorm informs the separated-alternative multiple-testing architecture but studies a different inverse-regression experiment. AamariAaronLevrard2021Boundary supplies background for positive reach and \(C^2\) embedded-manifold geometry and is the source for the positive-reach premise. It is not the source of the proposal's two-sided length envelope, injective \(C^{\iota+2}\) chart, uniform chart-derivative envelope, lower chart-speed bound, or arm-specific design-thickness condition.
technical_internal_limitation: The decision restriction is coordinatewise: \(\widehat{\tau}_n(x)\) may use \(U_{n,P}(x)\) but may not triangulate score locations from distances released at other boundary points. A joint multi-center release is a different experiment. Exact-radius conditionals are only determined almost everywhere: the canonical representative uses the coarea ratio where \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0\) and the existing H\"older representative \(\mu_{t,P}(x)\) otherwise. Two-sided thickness ensures only that positive-denominator radii accumulate at zero; it does not imply positivity at every radius. The angular-density packing must explicitly construct bounded continuous density perturbations whose imbalance varies at scale \(a_n\), verify common density, tail, variance, H\"older, assignment-partition, reach, and arm-mass constants, keep the straight geometry and affine regressions, and prove the stated compressed-law Kullback--Leibler and packing bounds. Rough density by itself is not a lower-bound proof. For fixed \(P\), the higher-order angular integrals in Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu, Theorem 3(ii), may be differentiable; the diagnostic point is only that no uniform derivative bound follows from this proposal's density envelope. The primitive class here and the anchor's nonparametric class are distinct, and no inclusion is asserted.
honest_scope: The theorem-level targets are rate equivalences, not exact asymptotic constants. Exact-distance conditional expectations are identified only up to null radial sets; the canonical coarea representative fills those radii with \(\mu_{t,P}(x)\), and H\"older continuity makes its boundary limit unique without assuming a positive circle denominator at every radius. The rectifiable result establishes the predicted logarithmic phenomenon only under the novel primitive two-sided design-thickness condition; the logarithmic frontier on the exact nonparametric class of Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu, Theorem 6, remains open. The smooth theorem concerns the fixed endpoint-trimmed target and uses no density modulus beyond continuity and fixed upper and lower bounds. Its lower bound has an explicit compressed-experiment construction obligation on a straight two-half-plane submodel with affine regressions. The full-location Stone exponent is stated only for the separately defined full-location decision class and is strictly faster than the distance exponent only when \(q>1\). The weakest empirically meaningful regularity producing a faster distance-only frontier is open.
